goal: Accessibility and text audit, touching only what a mouse-and-keyboard player would: every screen and panel; cut-off, overlapping, unclear or misspelled text; contrast; anything only explained on hover.

findings.title: In-settlement HUD: Inventory panel jumps to screen centre and Player Info panel is cut off by the bottom edge
findings.detail: After founding and entering the settlement, the Inventory Info panel moves from bottom-left to the middle of the screen (x~220,y~226), over the well and the 'Objective complete!' toast. The Player Info panel at bottom-right is clipped by the window edge: only Energy and 'Nation: Westville (LEADER)' show, and Relationships/Role/Facing/Land are gone. Expected the panels to stay docked and fully visible. Same displacement happens in the open world when the Era box is expanded (the Tip window then overlaps Inventory and cuts off 'Coins: 33[9]'; shots/era-expand-overlap.png).
findings.repro: pt start --seed 109; Start; Begin; chop to 50 wood; N; walk south out of range of other camps; F; E; Escape

findings.title: Settlement screen title and HUD top are overlapped by the huge world-space settlement label
findings.detail: Inside or near your own settlement, a large translucent white label ('0 here, 1/8 residents') is drawn across the top of the screen behind 'CAMP OF WESTVILLE', the status bar and the chronicle panel, so both become hard to read. The settlement screen text has no backing panel (for example 'Prices (buy/sell): ... Stone 30/28.' sits over the well roof). Expected the world label to be hidden or moved while UI is over it, and a backing panel behind screen text.
findings.repro: found a settlement (F), then press E at it

findings.title: Disabled action buttons explain themselves only on hover, and the tooltips cover the neighbouring buttons
findings.detail: Greyed buttons (Enter Settlement, Plant Sapling, Found Settlement, Build House, Build Stall, Trade at Market) give the reason only in a hover tooltip ('No settlement has been founded yet.', 'Needs 35 more wood.', 'Needs 17 more wood and 15 more stone...'). A keyboard player never sees these reasons. The tooltips also cover the button itself or the whole next row: Found Settlement's tooltip covers Leave Nation, Build House's covers the second row, and Trade at Market's covers the Player Info header.
findings.repro: in world: pt move 298 517 (Enter Settlement); after N: pt move 75 476; in settlement: pt move 233 413

findings.title: Objective progress bar uses white text on a yellow fill (~1.9:1)
findings.detail: The objective progress bar ('Wood 15/50', 'Wood 50/50') and the Village progress square are yellow (230,179,0) with white text on top, measured at 1.94:1 contrast. When the bar is full the label is almost unreadable. Expected dark text on the yellow, or a darker fill.
findings.repro: N to create nation; objective 4 'Found a settlement' bar

findings.title: Light-blue menu screens: white text on #73A6E6 is about 2.5:1 contrast
findings.detail: The title ('Press any key or click to continue'), the Config labels, the New World seed prompt, the main menu 'Last played: ...' line and the Load title are all small white text directly on the sky-blue background, measured at 2.52:1, below WCAG AA (4.5:1). The dark-blue buttons themselves read fine.
findings.repro: pt start; observe title, main menu, Config

findings.title: Config options have no explanation or tooltip; desktop Volume label says sound only works in the browser
findings.detail: 'Chunk Size', 'Location Scale', 'Lag Prevention' and 'Respawn Pawns' show nothing when hovered (waited 2s), so a player cannot tell what they do or what they cost. 'Volume (sound plays in the browser version)' on the desktop build tells the player that sound does not play here, but Volume and Mute controls are still offered.

findings.title: Chronicle lines truncated with '...' and no way to read them in place
findings.detail: Most recent-chronicle lines are cut off ('...declared the nation of Villageton, t...', and the player's own 'You raised a banner and named your people We...'). Hovering does not expand them; you have to press Y. The full Chronicle window (Y) is translucent, so the HUD panels behind it show through its text, and its header reads '4 entries. Listing 2.', which is unclear. 'Your news' also lists other nations' foundings while the player has no nation.
findings.repro: chop a few trees; observe chronicle; pt key y

findings.title: Red 'Leave Nation' appears in the exact slot 'Create Nation' just occupied, with no warning
findings.detail: Pressing N re-flows the action bar: a red 'Leave Nation' button takes the bottom-left spot where 'Create Nation' was a moment earlier, and hovering it gives no warning about consequences. The nation is also auto-named ('Westville') with no naming prompt.
findings.repro: pt key n; observe bottom-left; pt move 90 517

findings.title: Floating gain text (+5 wood etc.) has no outline; 2.2-3.2:1 over grass
findings.detail: The floating '+2 saplings', '+2 apples' and '+5 wood' after chopping are light green or brown text with no outline over green grass and the trunk. Measured 2.2:1 for brown '+5 wood' and 3.2:1 for green. The 'Objective complete!' toast is also drawn on top of these floats ('+3 apples', '+50 coins'), hiding them.
findings.repro: pt walkto tree; pt key e; pt shot

findings.title: 'Send Caravan (Village era)' is drawn as enabled although the era is locked
findings.detail: In the Camp era the Send Caravan button uses the enabled blue style, unlike the other unavailable buttons, and clicking it only shows an error. That 2-line status ('This settlement needs a Storehouse...') overlaps and hides the chronicle header '[Y: more]'.
findings.repro: inside settlement in Camp era; pt click 560 413

findings.title: HUD 'Village: 0/4', yellow square and Era '+' are unlabelled and have no tooltip
findings.detail: Nothing tells the player what 'Village: 0/4' counts, what the yellow square is, or that 'Era: Camp (1/4) +' can be clicked. Clicking it shows a good checklist ('To reach the Village era...'). Controls page 2 calls it 'Era box (tap)', which is touch wording on desktop.

findings.title: Settlement screen wording is self-contradictory and buttons are vague
findings.detail: 'Residents: 1 of 8 (0 here now). You are inside it.' contradicts itself. 'Give it to yourself to keep it if the rule passes on' is hard to parse, and the 'Give to: you' selector is grey on grey. The screen has both 'Exit Settlement' and 'Back', and the HUD has a plain 'Settlement' button (which reopens this screen). 'Purchase Food', 'Sell Resources' and 'Withdraw Funds' have no tooltip giving cost or effect.

findings.title: Load screen 'Delete' button styled like the load button and flush against it
findings.detail: 'Delete' uses the same dark-blue style directly beside the save row, with no danger colour and no tooltip. (Not clicked, so whether it asks for confirmation is untested.) The pause menu has no Load, only the main menu does; that is fine, but the brief expected it in the pause menu.

findings.title: Objective 'Eat something' completes without the player eating
findings.detail: While chopping, an apple was eaten automatically ('Ate an apple (+15 energy).' at tick 1256). Objective 2 then completed 48 ticks after it began, so the Eat Apple button is never taught.
findings.repro: pt walkto tree; pt key e (a few times)

findings.title: Controls help spends page 3 of 3 on debug cheat keys
findings.detail: F1-F6 (spawn pawn, coins, wood, teleport all pawns) are listed in the player-facing help with no note that they are debug cheats.

findings.title: Inventory screen (I) shows less than the HUD
findings.detail: With items at 0, the full Inventory screen shows only 'Coins: 339' and the close hint, drawn over the world and the player model with no panel. The HUD panel already lists every resource.

verdict: The text itself is well written (clear objectives, actionable errors like 'Open ground lies about 70 paces to the south', no typos), but layout and contrast let it down. Panels move when the HUD changes (Inventory jumps to the centre, Player Info gets clipped in settlements), the huge world-space settlement label sits behind the UI, and the reasons buttons are disabled live only in hover tooltips that cover other buttons. Contrast fails on the light-blue menus (~2.5:1), the white-on-yellow progress bar (1.9:1) and the floating gain text.
